locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the channel implementations treat the arguments passed to NotificationChannel.send? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: EmailChannel appends the unsubscribe footer by assigning to msg.body, mutating the OutboundMessage that Notifier passes to every channel in turn. If email is not delivered (retryable or rejected) and Notifier falls back to SMS, the SMS text now carries the email footer, eating into the length limit. Callers that reuse the message object (for example a retry of notify) get the footer appended again each time. The channel should build a local string; the interface could also take Readonly<OutboundMessage> to make this a compile error.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Channels are [push, email, sms]. Push's send throws a network error. What happens next?
choices: notify rejects with the network error
The attempt is recorded as retryable and Notifier moves on to email
Notifier retries push until it succeeds
Push is recorded as rejected and no further channels are tried
choiceQuestions.explanation: Notifier wraps channel.send in try/catch, converts any thrown error into a retryable outcome, records it, and continues the loop to the next channel. It does not rethrow, retry the same channel, or stop.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A message with priority "low" is sent to a user whose email address is unknown (addressFor returns null). Channels are [email, sms]. What is in the returned report?
choices: channel: null with one rejected email attempt
channel: null and an empty attempts list
It throws because no channel could be used
choiceQuestions.explanation: Email is skipped before any attempt because the address is null, and SmsChannel.supports returns false for low priority, so it is skipped too. No attempts are recorded and channel stays null; nothing throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The SMS gateway returns status "failed" for a submit. How does that surface through the SendOutcome contract?
choices: As { kind: "retryable" }, so Notifier tries the next channel
As { kind: "rejected" }, so Notifier stops trying further channels
As a thrown error that Notifier logs
As { kind: "delivered" } because the gateway accepted the request
choiceQuestions.explanation: SmsChannel maps any non-queued status to retryable. Notifier continues on both retryable and rejected (it only stops on delivered), so the 'stops' part of the rejected option is wrong as well; nothing is thrown, and failed is not treated as delivered.
